plan.title: Bind status samples to prepared workload provenance

criteria.description: A POSIX preparation helper hashes the binary and complete synthetic workload (inputs, configuration and prepared evidence), records a canonical manifest, rejects unsafe paths/types and detects file set, content, identity and root/directory replacement changes. Metadata-only pre-sample validation does not read file content; post-sample hashing is outside timed collection. Regression tests prove mutation rejection and descriptor cleanup.

Warm/first-run measurement output binds each accepted sample to a single prepared manifest; actual small workload smoke verifies matching provenance, existing labels/units and cold-cache refusal. No reset backend or reader guard is enabled.
Existing measurement validation, collector failure and cache-label regression suite remains passing.

limitations: E03b-1 only: provenance detects observed changes, not a hostile same-user/root actor that restores files between observations. Metadata checks are not a proof of no prior reads or cold state. E03b-2 owns reader control and E03b-3 owns ordered reset/probe/start integration. POSIX provenance tests skip on Windows; native Linux runtime is verified separately from cross-platform vet. No new dependency, installation or cold-cache enablement. A manifest includes generated evidence metadata and its digest is not cross-run reproducibility or binary build attestation.
